correctness.rationale: For the nested ellipses K_a=(a cos t,sin t), the frozen exact boundary integral and its differentiated decomposition Fp prime=Np+Tp are valid for p>-1 and a>0. For p>=0 both radial weight and arc-length factor increase pointwise. For -1<p<0, Tp=O(a log(1/a))=o(a^p); after t=az, Np/a^p converges by an integrable uniform majorant to 2p sqrt(pi) Gamma((1-p)/2)/Gamma(1-p/2)<0. Integrating gives the exact negative coefficient Cp a^(p+1), and Fp prime(1)=pi(p+1)>0 forces an interior minimum. The affine horizontal contraction gives d_H(K_a,K_{a/2})=a/2, so the nonzero difference quotient rules out exponent>p+1 on this smooth nested family. Independent high-precision quadrature at p=-0.5,-0.25 and a=0.002 reproduced the predicted cusp coefficient within expected pre-asymptotic error. This does not claim global decrease, unique minimum, or new universal exponent.
